data.title: Poland: Police foils alleged assassination attempt against PM
data.description: Poland's interior ministry said Sunday a man had been detained on suspicion of plotting an attack against Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz. Interior minister Marcin Kierwinski told Polish media that the suspect, a man in his 60s, had been arrested in the southwestern region of Lower Silesia. He was identified through an analysis of content posted online. The man's home is being searched and his contacts examined. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Warsaw, Adrien Sarlat.

data.title: Fire destroys historic French market of Enfants-Rouges in Paris
data.description: The historic Marché des Enfants-Rouges in central Paris was gutted by fire early on Monday. The market in the Marais neighbourhood is the oldest covered market in the French capital, dating back to 1615, and is also a listed building. Firefighters say the blaze has been brought under control but that the premises have been severely damaged. Details by Caitlin Brown.

data.title: Are European automakers capable of withstanding Chinese competition?
data.description: The Paris Motor Show opens its doors today, and with it come mounting economic and diplomatic issues. The European Union has just announced that it has secured a commitment from China to moderate the flow of hybrid vehicles into the block's market. It opens the prospect of cutting China's export by more than a half and could prevent millions of Chinese cars from being shipped to Europe. Are European automakers capable of withstanding this competition and their dependence on China? This report from France 2 and Morgan Ayre.

data.title: At least 139 migrants die in boat wreck between Djibouti and Yemen
data.description: At least 139 migrants died, including 15 children and 84 went missing when an overcrowded boat sank on its way from Djibouti to Yemen on the night between October 8 and 9. The International Organization for Migration said most of the people were Ethiopian when the vessel capsized off north of the town of Obock. Details by Morgan Ayre.

data.title: Zelensky says surprised to hear about Trump's 'energy ceasefire' between Ukraine and Russia

data.title: Who is Raphael Glucksmann, winner of the French left presidential primary?
data.description: With just six months to go to presidential polls in France, a coalition of centre left parties have chosen their candidate… It's EU lawmaker, Raphael Glucksmann. The 46 year old tells voters he stands for a break with Macronism, a break with the far left of candidate Jean Luc Melenchon and that he's the candidate who can defeat the far right… though opinion polls suggest that in a second round run off he would not beat far right candidate Marine Le Pen.

data.title: France scrambles to deploy supply teachers, but will it be enough to quell student anger?

data.title: ‘We were not going to let this rapist destroy our lives’: how one couple came to terms with a devastating attack
data.description: After Susan Brison was raped and left for dead, her husband, Thomas, did his best to support her. They are still together, while many relationships collapse after a sexual assault. What did he get right – and wrong? And why did she want him to write about her ordeal? On a hot, still, silent noon, at a junction of dirt roads in rural France, Thomas Trezise stood scanning the horizon, looking and listening for his wife. He tried to soothe a deep foreboding. Susan Brison had headed out for a morning walk two hours ago. How could she be gone so long? This was 4 July 1990, the start of what was meant to be a busy summer. Trezise and Brison were both assistant professors in the US – he in French at Princeton and Brison in philosophy at Dartmouth – and had just arrived at the remote farmhouse of Trezise’s French colleague. Life seemed packed with promise. “I’d found someone with whom I really wanted to spend my life and I just felt very, very lucky,” says Trezise. “Susan and I had fallen quickly and deeply in love – it was magical – and at that point, we were also trying to conceive a child. We loved being in France. I kind of felt I’d found my way. It was a good place … until it happened.” Continue reading...

data.title: Fontaines DC: Dopamine Chamber review – gloomy, gorgeous and a gargantuan triumph
data.description: (XL) This is a beguiling, endlessly inventive and frequently astonishing fifth LP from a group at increasing ease with being the best band of their generation Fifteen centuries ago, the Byzantine archbishop Theophilus of Adana did first-hand business with the devil for his own superficial betterment. Today, we just blindly tick a little box marked “accept terms and conditions” or let high-street snake oil merchants inject poison into our faces. The Faustian pact has become as depressingly banal as it is endemic and destructive – and unlike Theophilus, we can’t rely on the Virgin Mary to save us now. In the midst of headlines about AI destroying humanity, the idea of listening to music submerged in precisely this shade of doom might sound like, well, hell. If anyone can thread that poisoned needle, it’s Fontaines DC. When the Dublin band introduced their last album, 2024’s Romance , it came with a surprise new look . Their uncoordinated jeans and shirts had been replaced by neon hair, shiny trousers and bug-eyed sunglasses that split the difference between Korn and the Prodigy. As they faced up to having traded their anonymity to become arena fillers, it wasn’t hard to read this look as a sort of protective cosplay, a cybergoth Sasha Fierce for five fairly low-key Irish lads trying to make peace with leaving their roots behind. Newly melodic and lavishly produced, Romance made no bones about the band’s ambitions and became their first platinum-certified album. Continue reading...

data.title: Time review – David Tennant’s furious drama is as important as Adolescence
data.description: The third series of Jimmy McGovern’s terrifying and acutely moving prison drama is set in a young offender institute – and the reality it depicts needs national attention Jimmy McGovern has said that this new, third instalment of his prison anthology drama Time will be the last. For the sake of audiences’ emotional equilibrium, you have to hope so. For the sake of scripted drama, for the sake of art that has a hope of stirring the conscience of authorities and effecting change, you have to hope not. This time, Time is inside a young offender institution. It is crammed with under-18-year-old males, locked up often for 23 hours a day, all subject to the relatively new “keep apart” system whereby prisoners deemed likely to be violent towards each other are not allowed out of their cells at the same time. Naturally, this leads to a lot more boys being banged up for a lot more of the day and suits the officers a lot better. It is a facet of modern YOIs that McGovern and his co-writer Sam Bailey, a man evidently cut from the same socially conscious cloth, are clearly intent on bringing to wider attention. Their script, and the direction by Paul Whittington, do a wonderful, terrifying job of conveying the kinetic energy pent up and desperate for release, and the seething fury ever threatening to erupt, in every scene. Continue reading...

data.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
data.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. data.title: ‘I want to do everything I can to head off dementia’: why demand for the shingles vaccine is soaring
data.description: Could a drug intended to prevent painful rashes also protect our brains as we get older? The signs are promising – but not conclusive. Yet that’s enough to be driving a boom in shingles jabs When Jenny, a 50-year-old marketing and branding professional from Cambridge, went for her shingles vaccine last year, an entirely different disease was on her mind. Having witnessed three of her four grandparents succumb to dementia, with all the distress that brought, she wants to avoid the same fate. She hopes the shingles vaccine might help. Jenny is far from alone. Britain’s high street chemists have reported a rise in demand for the shingles vaccine, at least some of which is driven by people more worried about dementia than shingles. And while the vaccine is free for some on the NHS , most under-65s pay around £450 for the full two doses. Continue reading...

data.title: The one change that worked: numb with grief, I sat in the dark, surrounded by strangers – and began to heal
data.description: Life had come crashing to a halt when I lost my brother. But in the cinema I found comfort and a strange solidarity In 2022, my younger brother drowned in an accident. His death reset life as I knew it. I had been offered my first proper job; I didn’t take it. I was planning to move out; I stayed at home. At this critical juncture, with my foot on the pedal, ready to enter adult life, everything exploded. At home, there were now three of us. We orbited separate corners of the house, each needing a different thing for comfort: for my mum, exercise; for my dad, music; for me, escape. Continue reading...

data.title: Mort la révolution! Why UK film loves a failed rebellion
data.description: Paul Greengrass’s Peasants’ Revolt epic, The Uprising, is just the latest in a long line of movies depicting an unsuccessful attempt at remaking the nation The British are perverse. We fetishise our failures, even if they are essentially tangential to a national narrative that should be about imperial conquest, slavery and being unremittingly unpleasant to foreigners. We tell and retell, for instance, the story of Captain Scott even though he died in Antarctica in 1912 after losing the race to reach the south pole first to the unacceptably Norwegian Roald Amundsen. Similarly, Christopher Nolan’s 2017 film Dunkirk typified the British tendency to snatch national glory from the jaws of defeat. And then there was the tragicomic disaster of the Charge of the Light Brigade during the 1853-56 Crimean war in which our boys raced to putatively glorious if stupid deaths. It’s as if, for us British, pointless sacrifice and embracing failure are what heroism means. And our cinema has colluded with this perversity. But there is an exception to this national veneration of failure. Britain has been reluctant to embrace its revolutionary defeats. There is, for instance, no film dealing with the Chartist movement’s 19th-century struggle for universal suffrage. Even more strikingly yet, it is only now, in 2026, that a film has been made about the calamitous 1381 Peasants’ Revolt, even though it is a pivotal event in British history. Paul Greengrass’s The Uprising , starring Andrew Garfield as a – let’s just get this over with – revolting peasant, joins a mere handful of other movies, including Kevin Brownlow and Andrew Mollo’s 1975 Winstanley , Bill Douglas’s 1986 Comrades and Mike Leigh’s 2018 Peterloo , that dare depict how radical collective action was crushed by a ruthless state. Continue reading...

data.title: Is it true that … muscle turns into fat if you stop working out?
data.description: If you take a break from the gym you may lose muscle and gain fat, but it isn’t as simple as one turning into the other ‘This is not true,” says Prof Leigh Breen, a specialist in muscle physiology at the University of Leicester. But it’s a statement he hears a lot, particularly from people who have taken a long break from exercise. “They’ll often refer to the notion that their muscles have ‘softened’ or don’t feel as toned.” The reality is that there’s no biochemistry linking the two types of tissue. Muscle and fat are distinct. “There’s no known process in the human body that would support muscle turning into fat, or vice versa,” says Breen. Continue reading...

data.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Pumpkin, the rescue cat turned social media star
data.description: Struggling to breathe, so big she could barely walk, Pumpkin practically begged for help when we met. Before long I was taking her home Pumpkin arrived at our animal shelter in March, after her owner passed away. As CEO and president of SPCA Cincinnati, I expect something heartbreaking when my team asks me to see an animal – perhaps they have been neglected or abused. Pumpkin was neither. She was dirty and had some fleas but that was not our concern. She was severely obese. At 25lb (11.3kg), Pumpkin could barely move. Her legs were bowed from the weight and she walked with a waddle. Examining her wasn’t easy. Her breathing became so laboured that she turned blue. Continue reading...

data.title: Peasants by Maryam Aslany review – why an ancient way of life may hold the key to our future
data.description: Modernity means cities – or so we’re told. This bold new study of those who make their living from the land argues otherwise The word “peasant” has a negative edge: it has come to mean someone ignorant, unsophisticated, lowborn. Such an attitude, writes Maraym Aslany in this impressive piece of anthropology-cum-history, is “a residue of the massive psychodrama which made us who we are … we became modern by expelling the peasant parts of ourselves”. Her book weaves together a global history of peasants and an account of the four years she spent travelling in India, Cambodia, Peru and Ghana, living with and talking to peasant families. She aims to challenge the notion that the decline of the peasantry is the necessary condition for becoming “modern”. This notion arose in Britain, the first country to rid itself of its peasants when, with the enclosure acts, it turned its land from a common good into a financial asset. As this model of capitalist modernity began to take over the world, intellectuals of every stripe argued that peasants stood in the way of “progress”. Voltaire saw them as slow-witted people unable to understand their piteous state, stumbling blocks in the pursuit of enlightenment. Karl Marx believed that their “relentless property fanaticism” made them a reactionary element within capitalism. Continue reading...

data.title: The Gulf has entered a new era of instability. If its leaders think they can rely on old alliances, they are wrong | Nesrine Malik
data.description: The latest attack by Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia may prove to be more calamitous for the region than the world imagines On Saturday, Houthi rebels launched a shocking and deadly attack on Saudi Arabia’s capital city, Riyadh. At the time of writing, the missile strike on King Khalid international airport has killed at least 13 people and left 300 injured, marking a significant turn in a regional conflagration that is only getting more intense. It was the single most deadly attack on any Gulf country since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. In Saudi Arabia, a country that is unaccustomed to such fatalities, the death toll is bewilderingly high and likely to prompt a bloody response. Over the past year, the Gulf has entered a new era of instability that is not temporary and cannot be reversed. This may feel like an overstatement – casualties have been relatively low, after all, compared with Gaza and Iran – but the gradual erosion of peace and security in places such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE has changed the region more dramatically than its leaders would like to acknowledge. Nesrine Malik is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: I don’t have children. So who will I leave my precious possessions to when I die? | Kiran Sidhu
data.description: The quirky vase, the owl candlestick, my mother’s ring – these items hold part of me and carry with them an existential problem A friend of mine recently discussed his will with me. He talked about the importance of looking after his daughter financially when he’s gone. As a child-free woman, I confidently told him my money will go to organisations that have meant something to me: Macmillan Cancer Support and animal charities. It bemuses me how people think the absence of children is a problem when it comes to inheritance money; it’s always been obvious to me that I’d give my money to causes that touch my heart. But then my friend served something of a curveball. He asked me who will have my deceased mother’s ring? It made me think: where do the precious artefacts from our lives go when we are no longer here? Whenever I’m away from home I look forward to being reunited with these things: the quirky vase that sits in the window of my study, and the owl candlestick, a birthday gift from my potter friend. These items carry parts of me – what will become of them? If you have children, the answer to this question is not presented to you as a puzzle; like a constellation of stars, the answer is perfectly aligned. If you don’t have children, the question can lead to existential angst. Kiran Sidhu is a freelance journalist and writer. She is the author of I Can Hear the Cuckoo. She also wrote the Bafta award-winning documentary Heart Valley. Continue reading...

data.title: Autumn is here, and I’ve got five micro-moments of joy to see us through
data.description: For those of us who don’t like the chilly seasons, ‘glimmers’ are the way to go. This year mine are woolly, furry, scaly and crunchy It finally got cold and dark in my neighbourhood last week. While that’s just how I like it, I know not to alienate summer people by celebrating: screw crunchy leaves, soup, cosy sweaters, got it. I do, actually, sort of get it: fat bear week is over, decay is in the air, we’re dreading what El Niño might do, and somewhere, some content creator is plotting to ruin sofa season with an awful new self-optimisation concept (“Forget the winter arc , lock in for the Shackleton shred: a single rusk and 14-hour sled-pull daily for three months!”). It’s time to find some “glimmers”, which is what we’re calling little fragments of cheer now. “Micro moments of happiness that can flip the script on your day” have gone “pretty mainstream”, Grazia magazine said last month, but if you missed the memo, me too. I was busy spiralling into heatwave-fuelled existential dread when trend forecasters explored the glimmer concept this spring – it’s been a low-glimmer time for me. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on mental health: overdiagnosis is not the problem facing young people | Editorial
data.description: Parity of esteem with physical healthcare remains a distant prospect. Ministers must do more to tackle rising distress Perhaps the single most important finding of the independent review into mental health, ADHD and autism in England, published last Friday, is that mental distress across the population, and particularly young people, has substantially worsened . Its chair, Prof Peter Fonagy, told the BBC that the former health secretary Wes Streeting had been “completely wrong” to suggest that conditions and disorders were being overdiagnosed. Mr Streeting acknowledged his mistake. But some rightwing politicians and commentators have leapt on the notion that medicalisation of ordinary states of mind is behind the huge rise in young people seeking help. This review should bury that idea. Instead, this should be a moment to face facts. First, that the rises in psychological distress, and the need for support with neurodevelopmental differences , are real and tied to social changes. Second, that current services are not up to what is being asked of them. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on the US, Russia and the international criminal court: Trump’s assault on the rule of law intensifies | Editorial
data.description: A fuel deal with Vladimir Putin, and sanctions against the legal institution, ram home the president’s belief that might is right On Friday, Donald Trump drove home his belief that might is right and the rule of law is an obstacle rather than an essential foundation stone of international order. First came the escalated assault on the international criminal court (ICC) , sanctioning the body itself. Then he announced a deal with Russia to buy diesel. The US has long chafed at the notion of being bound by the rule of law that it espoused publicly. That hypocrisy now appears as a lesser vice. The president has declared that “my own morality” is all that constrains him. His brazen flouting of the law, embrace of dictators and rhetorical attacks all undermine global standards. data.description: The 21-year-old goalkeeper wants to impress on football the need to change old habits for the sake of the planet “I’m a bit of an outlier as a person, I like being unique in who I am and what I do,” says the former Arsenal goalkeeper Alexéi Rojas, who combines saving shots with saving the planet. “I would say that was one of the biggest pulls for me to become a goalkeeper. data.title: The Deshaun Watson revival derailed, much to the joy of those with a functional memory
data.description: After three straight game-winning drives, Cleveland’s quarterback was sacked eight times in a dismal defeat that punctured the hype surrounding him I guess the New York Jets didn’t get the memo. This was supposed to be a Deshaun Watson lovefest. A day where, much to the chagrin of those of us with a moral compass and a functional memory , football fans worldwide could declare Watson was “so back” and that the Browns were in some blinkered, alternate universe, a Super Bowl contender. No such luck, as the Browns looked like the Browns – reminding an otherwise jubilant city of Cleveland that they are trapped in the sports equivalent of the Backrooms. Limping along for 155 passing yards and one touchdown, Watson fell to Earth harder than David Bowie in a Nicolas Roeg film (yes, I just watched the Dennis Miller Monday Night Football documentary on HBO). He completed fewer than 50% of his passes and ended the day with a 69.6 passer rating. I should also probably mention he got sacked eight times. Yes, eight times. EIGHT TIMES . He only completed seven more passes than he received punishing hits behind the line of scrimmage. It was a performance NBC NFL writer Patrick Daugherty called “ unspeakably bad .” Actually, I think the performance was very much speakable, as I’ve demonstrated here. Stick around for another 400 words. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘That’s when I begin to scream’: Mick Fanning on punching a great white shark
data.description: The Australian surfing champion was monstered by a great white shark while competing against fellow Aussie Julian Wilson in the 2015 world tour event final at Jeffreys Bay in South Africa. The attack was broadcast live on TV. Here, in an extract from his memoir, All Heart, he relives the encounter I’m locked in on my take-off spot in the J-Bay lineup, scanning the horizon, biding my time. Assessing my position against the rippling lines of the oncoming set, I decide to move slightly further inside. As I move, there’s a big splash behind me. Glancing over my left shoulder, I catch a glimpse of a huge dark shape in the water. A jolt of fear grips me. What the hell is that? Continue reading...

data.title: Why a Chilean salt flat is a microcosm of the extractive frontiers of green capitalism
data.description: In the Atacama desert, the extraction of lithium – so crucial to addressing the climate crisis – comes with escalating social and environmental costs A high-altitude desert plateau traverses Argentina, Bolivia and Chile. I am on the Chilean side, sitting in a Jeep along with two other researchers. The afternoon air is thin and brisk but the sun is piercing – a combination I am familiar with from years of living and travelling in South America’s Andean range. The landscape is a study in contrasts and contours: broad basins suddenly cut off by sweeping curves; flat expanses sliced by near vertical ascents. The Licancabur volcano looms large above us. Vegetation and humidity levels change rapidly with the rising altitude, bringing cooler temperatures, wetter air and denser plant life. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A rare indulgence’: why Black Swan is my feelgood movie
data.description: The latest in our series of writers explaining their go-to comfort films is a tribute to Darren Aronofsky’s dark and unusually satisfying ballet nightmare In early 2011, sometime after the film was released on home video, I sat down with mum to watch what she had heard was a “new ballet movie” by Darren Aronofsky . I was 12 years old, spending school nights training to be a professional dancer. Without any warmup, knowing very little of the ballet and pointe work that earned Natalie Portman her best actress Oscar, we pressed play on Black Swan . Well before Brendan Fraser’s time on the couch and the many houseguests of Mother! , Aronofsky increased the wattage with a companion piece to follow his heavy-hitter, The Wrestler. Watching Nina Sayers’ (Portman) intense physical trials and her stilted sexual awakening, with my mum beside me, I was understandably disturbed. At this point in my adolescence, I thought Jumanji was a scary movie. Like the film’s injured bird, I was being introduced to a darkness I didn’t understand. And somehow I couldn’t get enough. Why did it feel so good? Continue reading...

data.title: Gabrielle Goliath: Elegy review – devastating lament is a furious, single-note call to action
data.description: Ibraaz, London Too controversial for the Venice Biennale, this haunting video and audio work commemorates murders and genocides with an angry act of mourning The sound of mourning spills out into the streets. A single, endless wailing note echoes out of the basement of Ibraaz, a relatively new cultural centre in London’s Fitzrovia. This is Gabrielle Goliath’s heart-wrenching Elegy, each of its three films featuring a woman singing just one note until their lungs falter and another woman steps up to fill in for her. Just as a note is about to die, it is sustained. It’s a haunting, shocking act of mourning for murder, injustice and genocide. And it almost never made it. Continue reading...

data.title: Hallowarrior review – apocalyptic Home Alone-style survival horror delivers inventive shocks
data.description: Debut feature from Ben Sottak provides outlandish Halloween-based scares, with Milly Shapiro superb as the naive yet resilient home-defender, Pumpkin Home Alone meets Mad Max in this atmospheric seasonal chiller, named for Halloween and not a cheery greeting. A disease has wiped out most of humanity, leaving 16-year-old Pumpkin (Milly Shapiro) stranded alone in her rural family home in the middle of nowhere for the best part of four years. This classic American clapboard house has always been the perfect quaint yet unsettling place to celebrate Halloween, and she determines to uphold the family tradition and do just that, sending a radio broadcast to anyone listening to invite them to celebrate spooky season with her. Unfortunately, the message is picked up by some less than wholesome types, led by Thalia (Shannyn Sossamon), thus setting the stage for the proverbial to hit the fan. It’s the first major screen role for Shapiro since her memorable debut as the little sister in Ari Aster’s Hereditary , and she is in almost every scene here, making for quite the showcase. It’s good casting: Pumpkin is an intriguing presence – at once young and old, presumably because she’s been fending for herself during such a key stage of her development. She’s not had any adult guidance since the age of 12 – arresting her development in some ways, while having to survive, be totally independent and grieve her entire family alone has simultaneously made her unusually tough in others. data.title: A Fidai Film review – Palestinian collage film transforms suppressed footage into works of art
data.description: Using archive material of destroyed houses, terrorised children and dead bodies, Kamal Aljafari adds humanity to the reels by overlaying poems by Palestinian authors In Arabic, “fidai” means someone willing to sacrifice themselves for the greater good. Borrowing this word, which is at times used in a military context, for his collage film, Palestinian film-maker Kamal Aljafari stages a potent uprising of images against the tide of propaganda and historical erasure. Much of the film draws on archive materials once housed in the Palestine Research Centre in Beirut. In 1982, during the Lebanese civil war, Israeli forces raided the centre and seized the archive. Most of these documents on Palestinian history – books, newspapers, audiovisual artefacts – are believed to still be in the hands of the Israeli army. Obtained through clandestine means, the footage that resurfaces in Aljafari’s film bears the physical traces of political suppression. The images are scratched, grainy and pixelated, yet through the power of montage they evoke startling visual parallels that point to the relentless violence endured by Palestinians through the decades. Black-and-white film taken during the British mandate show soldiers patrolling the streets and inflicting violence upon the Indigenous population; similar acts then committed by Israeli forces. In place of a chronological order, the editing builds a sense of continuity through recurring images. Time and time again, we see torn-down houses, terrorised children and the bodies of Palestinians murdered by occupation forces. Continue reading...

data.title: Deadline review – shocking threat sends tremors through authoritarian school
data.description: Set in a dystopian private academy rife with surveillance and cut-throat competition, Kiwi Chow’s gripping drama cements his status as an important film-maker Filmed in Taiwan and set entirely inside a prestigious high school, Kiwi Chow’s gripping drama frames educational systems not merely as a preparation for the real world but as a microcosm of society at large. At this elite private institute, pupils studiously march in lines like obedient soldiers, their purple uniforms the only pop of colour in a grey building of glass and steel. The school’s operations have a touch of dystopian sci-fi: students check in with AI recognition panels, which also display their class standing and disciplinary scores. In this sterile environment where human worth is measured by standardised metrics, the breathing room for individuality is nil. This panopticon atmosphere of surveillance and cut-throat competition is punctured by a shocking incident: an anonymous student drops a flurry of leaflets announcing their intent to take their own life on the day of the final exam, unless the school changes its authoritarian ways. The note sends tremors through both the administration and the students; intersecting narrative lines weave through a group of characters that include a model student, a dedicated but ambivalent teacher and a righteous slacker. Each carries a heavy secret that points to the moral rot beneath the facade of academic excellence. Continue reading...

data.title: The Party review – this pacey, perfectly cast thriller is enormous fun
data.description: Sarah Soleman’s adaptation of Elizabeth Day’s bestseller is hugely moreish – it leaves you absolutely desperate to find out more about the mystery at its heart Imagine going to a huge party in a country pile stuffed with posh Tory MPs. Now imagine being massively pregnant and unable to drink. Now imagine that the party is “Victorian freak show” themed, because the hostess thought that would be even more fun. Such is the situation Lucy Gilmour (Sarah Solemani) finds herself in at the beginning of The Party, Solemani’s adaptation of Elizabeth Day’s 2017 bestseller of the same name. When you learn that a gun has gone off, your first thought may well be that this can only improve matters. At the very least, the circus troupe will probably decline to perform further, and I believe even posh people have to stop conga-ing to 80s hits once the police show up. Like most of us, I’d be tempted to fire the gun into the air myself. Continue reading...

data.title: The Weight of Angels by John Boyne review – what if Oscar Wilde had lived?
data.description: The great Irish writer died, a broken man, at only 46. Imagining a second act for him is a great idea – but the results are sentimental and unconvincing In 1895, four days after the opening of The Importance of Being Earnest, the Marquess of Queensberry left a card at Oscar Wilde’s club that publicly accused him of “posing as a somdomite”. Instead of instigating the libel case that led to his imprisonment and early death in a Paris hotel just five years later, what would have happened if Wilde had simply torn that card up? John Boyne’s new novel sets out to answer that intriguing question. For starters, Boyne contrives a fate for Wilde’s beloved Lord Alfred Douglas which entertainingly redistributes the details of the real Wilde’s life before, during and after his time in Reading jail. This sets up the novel’s cat-and-mouse game with the history it is reimagining. Wilde himself, conveniently released from marriage by the early death of his wife, is then free to live not as a tortured, scandal-haunted genius, but as a randy, wisecracking, party-going queen. The upside of this is that Oscar gets to swap bons mots with a crowded cast list of celebrities; the downside is that he shows little sign of the troubled and radical mind that produced the real Wilde’s late journalism and fiction, never mind the subversive linguistic pyrotechnics of The Importance. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We’re in a brotherhood now’: the Bill Pickett rodeo – photo essay
data.description: For several years, Chloe Kerleroux has been photographing African American cowboy communities in the southern US. Her work has mainly focused on trail rides: large gatherings where horses, music, dancing, family and community life come together. This year, she explored rodeo culture including at the Bill Pickett invitational in Atlanta The image of the cowboy widely portrayed in westerns and popular culture has long been almost exclusively white. Yet Black cowboys hold an important place in the history of the American west. After the civil war and the abolition of slavery, many African Americans found work on ranches and on the great cattle drives westward. By the late 19th century, historians estimate about one in four cowboys were Black. Among the Black figures who shaped this history was Bill Pickett . Born in Texas in 1870, he became one of the most celebrated Black cowboys and rodeo performers of his time, known in particular for popularising bulldogging, which would eventually give rise to modern steer wrestling. After the national anthem, Josh, a member of the Outlaws Most Wanted, rides around the arena to a pounding hip-hop track as his teammates cheer him on at the Bill Pickett invitational rodeo in Conyers, near Atlanta, Georgia, on 2 August 2026 Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Enough of this suffering!’ Joana Vasconcelos on why she is fed up with women’s art defined by pain
data.description: The Portuguese artist is famous for her monumental ceramic wedding cakes and gigantic chandeliers made of tampons. So why is a new show in Lisbon pairing her with Valentino’s size-zero catwalk dresses? To interview the Portuguese artist Joana Vasconcelos is to jump on to a moving train. She is telling me why she uses needlework to make huge things: 15-metre doilies, say, or a tree 13.5 metres tall rustling with 150,000 hand-sewn leaves. “One day, I said to myself,” she says, “why not bring domestic detail into monumental sculpture? What do we know of works like this? OK, there’s Louise Bourgeois. But it wasn’t enormous. She worked in detail but on small things. There’s the beauty of Niki de Saint Phalle. But it’s always papier mache – a technique that’s very simple, very practical, but not chic.” It takes a certain something to compare yourself to these two French giantesses of art. It takes something else to castigate Bourgeois and de Saint Phalle for not being big, bold and beautiful enough. But if there’s one female contemporary artist who can do it without coming across as delusional, it’s Vasconcelos. Born in Paris in 1971 into an artistic Portuguese family, Vasconcelos has established herself as one of her country’s leading contemporary artists – and one of the world’s most ambitious. data.title: Calum Franklin’s recipes for balti paratha pie with spicy green chutney
data.description: A pleasingly proper curry-filled pie with a zingy chutney to go with it This is one of my all-time favourite pies, pie born out of the Midlands. While studying at University College Birmingham, the now head of department at the college of food there, Lewis Walker, and I were in digs together and regularly ended up in very late-night balti houses after big nights out. These pies remind me of that really special time. It wasn’t much before my university days when balti cooking emerged in 1970s Birmingham, apparently created as a way to appease the British palate of the time. Its roots are in Pakistani-Kashmiri cooking and the base of the curry always has to contain tomatoes, onions, peppers and chillies, although variations can be built on those foundations. They’re a wonderful celebration of multicultural Britain. Continue reading...

data.title: The kindness of strangers: In one of my darkest periods, a few compassionate words helped turn my life around
data.description: I was standing at the traffic lights with the weight of the world on my shoulders when a man approached. It was one of the darkest periods of my life, on seemingly every front: I was in the midst of a divorce; it was during the global financial crisis and the company I worked for was badly struggling, making every day feel heavy with uncertainty and stress. Everything was a mess and I was emotionally exhausted. One morning during rush hour, I stood at the traffic lights waiting to cross on my way to the office. I was lost in my thoughts but must have looked like I had the weight of the world on my shoulders, because something unexpected happened. Continue reading...

data.title: A lakeside idyll: laid-back cycling and autumn hikes on Italy’s Lake Iseo
data.description: Smaller and less visited than Como and Garda, Lake Iseo harbours a gorgeous car-free island ideal for easy-going cycling and sightseeing Rust red and burnt sienna speckle the green mountain rising from Lake Iseo. Golden autumn sunlight shimmers on the water. Monte Isola, Italy’s largest lake island, is a peak of sheer cliffs and dense forest, dotted with old fishing hamlets and hillside villages, each as pretty as the terraced villas of Lake Como and Garda, but with far fewer visitor s . I arrive at the small port town of Peschiera Maraglio – where striped wooden boats jut from the water like the gondolas of Venice – on a ferry from Sulzano, a five-minute hop across the water. “Only three people on the island are allowed to own a car: the priest, the doctor and the mayor,” says Chiara, my tour guide from Brescia. Residents can zip up and down the steep island roads on mopeds, and a small fleet of van-sized buses trundle around throughout the day, but nearly all cars are forbidden and visitors have to explore on foot or bike. Continue reading...

data.title: Ohio approves easements for 58 farms covering 5,165 acres as protected farmland tops 111,000 acres
data.description: Ohio has greenlit local sponsors to secure agricultural easements on 58 family-owned farms, aiming to safeguard farmland from non-agricultural development. Through the Local Agricultural Easement Purchase Program, farmers can keep cultivating their land while ensuring its preservation. Presently, more than 111,000 acres across 62 counties are safeguarded from development. With federal funding poised to enhance these efforts, local sponsors can apply for the 2027 program for further conservation.

data.title: A study of 77 Bronze Age children in Serbia found sex-linked burial customs dating back 4,000 years
data.description: The study of burial practices in Bronze Age Serbia indicates that children’s funerary treatment varied by biological sex, with research focused on two Maros culture cemeteries. This work sheds light on the nuances of how ancient communities perceived and enacted gender distinctions in funerary rituals.

A comprehensive strategy is essential to harmonize health measures with ecological integrity.

data.title: Inclusão produtiva é desafio que exige respostas coletivas
data.description: Há desafios grandes demais para uma empresa tentar atuar de forma isolada. A inclusão produtiva é um deles. Apesar dos avanços, 48,9 milhões de brasileiros ainda viviam em situação de pobreza em 2024. Segundo a SIS (Síntese de Indicadores Sociais) 2025, do IBGE , 8,6 milhões de pessoas saíram dessa condição entre 2023 e 2024, mas a pobreza ainda alcançava 23% da população. Por trás desse número está um desafio muito complexo. Em um país de realidades econômicas e sociais tão diferentes, ampliar oportunidades de trabalho e geração de renda exige mais do que recursos: exige criar condições para que essas atividades se desenvolvam de forma sustentável e ampliem a autonomia de quem está na ponta. Leia mais (10/12/2026 - 08h00)

data.title: Europa mit drittwärmstem September seit Aufzeichnungsbeginn
data.description: Im September haben sich in Europa die ungewöhnlich warmen und trockenen Bedingungen des Sommers fortgesetzt. In Westeuropa war es gemeinsam mit dem September 2023 der wärmste September seit Beginn der Aufzeichnungen, wie der EU-Klimawandeldienst Copernicus mitteilte. Die Temperatur lag 2,51 Grad über dem Mittel der Jahre 1991 bis 2020.

data.title: Při brutálním útoku oběti vyřízl střeva. Důvodem mohlo být mumlání o zápachu

data.title: Vražda šumperské taxikářky: policie navrhla obžalobu, muži hrozí výjimečný trest
data.description: Kriminalisté ukončili vyšetřování případu zavražděné čtyřiačtyřicetileté taxikářky v Šumperku a pokusu vraždy dalších dvou lidí z letošního února. „Krajskému státnímu zástupci jsme předali spis s návrhem na podání obžaloby na devětatřicetiletého muže, kterému hrozí 15 až 20 let nebo výjimečný trest,“ informoval v pondělí mluvčí policistů v Olomouckém kraji Libor Hejtman.

data.title: Británii opouštějí miliardáři. Nelíbí se jim daně ani nálada ve společnosti

data.title: Rusové jsou z Trumpa nadšení, jeho příměří už porušili. USA dál hrozí Kyjevu
data.description: Na slova amerického prezidenta Donalda Trumpa o energetickém příměří mezi Kyjevem a Moskvou reagovali s překvapením i Rusové. Potěšila je však jeho výzva k nahrazení ukrajinského prezidenta Volodymyra Zelenského. Spojené státy tlačí na Ukrajinu, aby přestala s útoky na ruské rafinerie a hrozí jí i omezením americké pomoci. Zelenskyj tvrdí, že Ukrajina útoky na rafinerie přerušila, ale Rusko nedodrželo příměří.

data.title: Ryze romská kandidátka uspěla. Hlavně, ať se nehádáme, přeje si starosta
data.description: Romská kandidátka v Měrovicích nad Hanou na Přerovsku ve volbách uspěla a probojovala se do zastupitelstva. Z celkem patnácti mandátů získala dvě křesla a usedne do nich sedmadvacetiletá asistentka pedagoga a lídryně kandidátky KDU-ČSL Aneta Pompová (nez.) a její o pět let mladší sestra Klára, jež pracuje jako prodavačka. data.title: Zbořím zeď u ruského velvyslanectví. Čižinský bojuje peticí za část Stromovky
data.description: Starosta Prahy 7 Jan Čižinský před druhým kolem voleb do Senátu spustil petici za znovuzískání části Stromovky, která je od roku 1968 připojena k ruskému velvyslanectví. Po strhnutí zdi, která půlhektarové území obepíná, by ho rád poskytl k veřejnému užívání. Spor o území je v řešení už od roku 2021.

data.title: Dotační podvod voliče Vápenné neodradil. Hannigovo uskupení znovu vyhrálo volby
data.description: Ani trest starosty od vrchního soudu neodradil voliče Vápenné na Jesenicku od znovuzvolení Leoše Hanniga (TOP 09) do vedení obce. Hannig byl přitom měsíc před volbami z funkce odvolán, teď se ale na starostovskou židli možná opět vrátí - Hannigovo uskupení Srdcem pro Vápennou (TOP 09 + NK) získalo v patnáctičlenném zastupitelstvu pět mandátů a vyhrálo volby. Bude se ale vyjednávat, v počtu preferenčních hlasů skončil Hannig až celkově třetí.

data.title: Dohodnuto. V Liberci utvoří koalici Starostové s Lepším Libercem a LOL+Piráty, ANO v opozici

data.title: Investigadores da Faculdade de Ciências usam nanocorpos para travar processo associado ao Alzheimer
data.description: Um trabalho levado a cabo por investigadores da Faculdade de Ciências da Universidade de Lisboa descobriu que fragmentos de anticorpos conseguem bloquear diferentes etapas da agregação da proteína Tau, associada a doenças neurodegenerativas. Para já, não trata de uma terapêutica, por estar ainda em fase de investigação, mas pode ser um avanço significativo para futuros caminhos no tratamento da doença de Alzheimer.

data.title: Macau transfere 1,76 mil milhões de euros para cobrir défice do Fundo de Pensões
data.description: O Governo de Macau anunciou hoje a transferência de cerca de 15,9 mil milhões de patacas (1,76 mil milhões de euros) para cobrir o défice do sistema de pensões dos trabalhadores da função pública.

data.title: China sanciona ministros do Paraguai e Belize por apoio a relações diplomáticas com Taiwan
data.description: A China anunciou hoje sanções contra dois ministros do Paraguai e do Belize por apoiarem "obstinadamente" a manutenção de relações diplomáticas dos respetivos países com Taiwan, ilha cuja soberania é reivindicada por Pequim.

data.title: A new dawn for Didim
data.description: For centuries, the environs of Didim in Mid-Aegean Türkiye have carried the whisper of prophecy. It was here, at the monumental Temple of Apollo, that pilgrims once walked the Sacred Way from ancient Miletus to consult the oracle. Perched on a hill, overlooking the Maeander plain, Priene is one of the best-preserved sites of the Ionian league. Both Miletus and Priene still resonate with the impression of ancient times; one feels like walking through a time capsule. The mighty oracle of Apollon temple stands high and strong, as if whispering a secret, or maybe telling what will come next.

data.title: Six senators call for Trump administration to ‘immediately reverse course’ on Russian diesel plan
data.description: A bipartisan group of six senators has urged President Trump to reverse his decision to purchase diesel from Russia to lower fuel prices, arguing it contradicts existing U.S. law prohibiting Russian energy imports amid the ongoing war in Ukraine. The senators expressed concern that providing financial support to Russia undermines efforts to hold the country accountable for its aggression, highlighting the lack of congressional consultation before the announcement.

data.title: Comprendre le Kashambala : une pratique traditionnelle liée au deuil chez les Bafuliru du Sud-Kivu.
data.description: Identité culturelle est votre rendez-vous consacré à la découverte, à la préservation et à la valorisation des traditions, des coutumes et du riche patrimoine culturel des communautés de la République démocratique du Congo. Dans les sociétés traditionnelles africaines, de nombreuses pratiques coutumières structuraient autrefois la vie familiale et communautaire. Elles régissaient les relations sociales, la transmission des biens, ainsi que les mécanismes d’organisation et de solidarité au sein des familles.

data.title: Pacifique Ndagano, Mkurugenzi Mtendaji wa SMICO: Wafanya biashara wanao pokea mikopo jimboni Maniama wanalipa vizuri.
data.description: Elimu ya kifedha inaonekana kuzaa matunda huko Maniema. Kampuni ya mikopo midogo ya Kongo SMICO inaripoti kiwango cha kutolipa cha 0.6% tu miongoni mwa wajasiriamali ambao wamepokea mikopo yake. Kulingana na Mkurugenzi Mtendaji wa kampuni hiyo, matokeo haya yanaonyesha kujitolea kwa kuheshimu majukumu na uthabiti katika ulipaji wa mikopo, tabia inayoonekana kuwa ya kutia moyo kwa maendeleo ya kiuchumi ya jimbo hilo. Pacifique Ndagano, Mkurugenzi Mtendaji wa SMICO. Anazungumza na Florence Kiza Lunga.

data.title: La société civile salue la reddition de plusieurs dizaines de combattants aux FARDC au Kivu
data.description: Le coordonnateur de la Société civile du Congo (SOCICORDC), Kelvin Bwijа, salue ce lundi 12 octobre la reddition de plus de 80 combattants de groupes armés enregistrée au cours des trois derniers mois dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu. Selon ce défenseur des droits humains, ces redditions concernent notamment des éléments de l’AFC/M23, de Twiraneho, de Red Tabara et de leurs alliés.

data.title: Des kits de dignité distribués aux femmes vulnérables à Kalehe au Sud-Kivu
data.description: Une dizaine de femmes enceintes et de femmes qui viennent d’accoucher, en situation de vulnérabilité, ont reçu samedi 10 octobre des kits de dignité au Centre hospitalier Rambo, dans la zone de santé de Kalonge, territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu. Cette assistance a été organisée par le Club des Filles Reporters (CFR RDC) pour soutenir ces femmes et répondre à certains de leurs besoins essentiels.

data.title: Ebola à Butembo : le Parlement d’enfants alerte sur le manque d’eau dans plusieurs écoles
data.description: Le Parlement d’enfants de Butembo-Lubero appelle ce dimanche 11 octobre, les autorités administratives et sanitaires à renforcer les mesures de prévention contre la maladie à virus Ebola dans les établissements scolaires. Dans plusieurs écoles de Butembo, au Nord-Kivu, les dispositifs de lavage des mains restent inutilisables en raison du manque d’eau, d’après l’organisation.

data.title: L’ARSP déploie de nouveaux OPJ pour faciliter l’accès des Congolais aux marchés de sous-traitance
data.description: Vingt-quatre nouveaux officiers de police judiciaire (OPJ) de l’Autorité de régulation de la sous-traitance dans le secteur privé (ARSP) ont prêté serment samedi 10 octobre au Palais de justice de Kinshasa-Gombe. data.title: Après la démolition du marché Mzée Kabila, Kamalondo s’apprête à accueillir les commerçants délocalisés
data.description: Les travaux d’aménagement du marché de Kamalondo, dans la commune du même nom à Lubumbashi, se poursuivent avant l’installation des commerçants délocalisés à la suite de la démolition du marché Mzée Kabila. data.title: Goma-Gisenyi : de nouvelles restrictions aux frontières ravivent les craintes d’isolement
data.description: De nouvelles restrictions sont observées depuis le samedi 10 octobre aux postes frontaliers de la Petite et de la Grande Barrière entre Goma, en République démocratique du Congo (RDC), et Gisenyi, au Rwanda. En l’absence de communication officielle, plusieurs sources évoquent des mesures de prévention liées à l’épidémie d’Ebola. Ces dispositions suscitent des inquiétudes parmi les habitants de Goma, qui redoutent un nouvel isolement de la ville.

data.title: Sud de Madagascar : près de 3,7 millions de personnes menacées par une grave crise alimentaire
data.description: La situation alimentaire devient particulièrement préoccupante dans le Grand Sud de Madagascar. Alors que la période de soudure n'a pas encore commencé, plusieurs localités enregistrent déjà des cas sévères de malnutrition. Selon une enquête de l'AFP, relayée par Paris Match, près de 3,7 millions de Malgaches pourraient être confrontés à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë dans les prochains mois. Une perspective alarmante, dans un contexte marqué par la sécheresse, la hausse des prix et la (…) - Société

data.title: 18 groupes électrogènes russes pour renforcer la production de la JIRAMA
data.description: Le gouvernement accélère ses initiatives pour faire face à la crise énergétique. La JIRAMA a reçu l'ordre de procéder à l'acquisition de 18 groupes électrogènes auprès de Malmekhservice, une entreprise de droit russe. Cette opération, décidée dans le cadre de l'état d'urgence énergétique, sera réalisée sans appel d'offres. Chaque équipement devrait développer une puissance de 1 mégawatt, selon les indications d'un technicien de la compagnie nationale. Les installations permettraient ainsi (…) - Energie

data.title: Liste électorale : la CENI multiplie les inscriptions, mais comment éviter les doublons ?
data.description: La Commission électorale nationale indépendante (CENI) intensifie ses opérations d'inscription des électeurs à Madagascar. Après avoir installé des dispositifs à Ambohijatovo et au stade Maki d'Andohatapenaka, elle intervient désormais directement dans les administrations publiques. Cette stratégie vise à faciliter les démarches des citoyens dont les obligations professionnelles ne permettent pas de se présenter dans les bureaux habituels. data.title: Tabla de posiciones Liga Nacional de Honduras tras triunfo de Real España: ¡Bajan a Olimpia!
data.description: Real España comenzó con el pie derecho la era de su nuevo entrenador, el español Juan Ignacio Martínez . La Máquina triunfó por 0-1 contra el Estrella Roja de Danlí , en la novena jornada del Torneo Apertura 2026 de la Liga Nacional de Honduras. El equipo aurinegro salió del Estadio Marcelo Tinoco con la victoria en el bolsillo gracias a un solitario gol de Jeffrey Ramos , quien conectó de cabeza un tiro de esquina de Jhow Benavídez a los 11 minutos. Estrella Roja buscó el empate sin cesar animado por su público, pero Real España cerró bien sus filas y logró los tres puntos que lo devuelven a la parte alta de la tabla de posiciones del campeonato. Así, el Real España se ubica en el liderato de la clasificación con 21 puntos, bajando al Olimpia al segundo puesto con 20 unidades. Los merengues ganaron por 0-1 al Génesis y siguen presionando por el primer lugar. En el tercer lugar está el Marathón con 18 puntos después del empate 0-0 que protagonizó contra los Lobos de la UPNFM , mientras el Motagua es cuarto con 16 enteros en su casillero tras vencer 2-1 al CD Choloma . Olancho FC subió al quinto escalón de la tabla de posiciones tras su empate 1-1 contra el Atlético Independiente . Los Potros llegaron a 12 puntos, mientras el Génesis es sexto con 11 unidades. En el séptimo puesto está el Atlético Independiente con 10 puntos, el Estrella Roja, con la derrota, es octavo con 9 unidades, emparejado con el noveno Lobos de la UPN. Platense se encuentra en el décimo lugar con 8 unidades, el CD Choloma quedó penúltimo con 7 y en el sótano sigue el Juticalpa FC con 6.

data.title: Embajada de EE UU lanza nueva advertencia sobre las caravanas migrantes
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. La Embajada de Estados Unidos en Honduras volvió a advertir sobre los riesgos que enfrentan las personas que intentan llegar al país norteamericano a través de caravanas migrantes y aseguró que estos desplazamientos fracasarán. “No desperdicies tu dinero ni arriesgues tu vida. Los traficantes de personas mienten. Las caravanas fracasan. La frontera está cerrada para los inmigrantes ilegales. Cualquier persona que intente ingresar ilegalmente a Estados Unidos será detenida, deportada y procesada. No arriesgues tu futuro”, escribió la sede diplomática en sus redes sociales. La publicación estuvo acompañada de una ilustración de una caravana con la leyenda: “TODAS las caravanas de inmigrantes ilegales fracasarán”. El 7 de octubre, la Embajada de Estados Unidos publicó otro mensaje en el que afirmó que, bajo el gobierno del presidente Donald Trump, “ningún inmigrante ilegal está logrando cruzar la frontera sur”, independientemente de si las personas intentan ingresar al país en una caravana, por cuenta propia o mediante el pago a un traficante de personas. En esa publicación, la sede diplomática también advirtió: “Ningún inmigrante ilegal está logrando cruzar la frontera sur de Estados Unidos bajo la Administración Trump. Ya sea que le pagues a un traficante de personas, intentes cruzar por tu cuenta o te unas a una caravana, intentar llegar ilegalmente a Estados Unidos fracasarás, y serás deportado o procesado.  No arriesgues tu futuro”. El pasado 20 de septiembre, una caravana partió desde San Pedro Sula, Cortés, con cientos de hondureños que se dirigían a Estados Unidos en busca de mejores oportunidades de vida. A raíz de estos desplazamientos, la Embajada estadounidense ha reiterado en varias ocasiones que los hondureños que intenten ingresar de manera irregular a su territorio podrían ser retornados. Durante su intervención ante la Asamblea General de la Organización de las Naciones Unidas (ONU), el presidente hondureño Nasry Asfura atribuyó la promoción de las caravanas a personas que buscarían obtener beneficios económicos. “Es un tema complicado de hablar porque alguien lo promueve por negocio, si miran los datos, varios fueron detenidos en Guatemala y vienen de retorno”, dijo el mandatario. De acuerdo con las autoridades del Instituto Nacional de Migración (INM), las deportaciones de hondureños podrían alcanzar los 50,000 casos al cierre de 2026. La mayoría de los retornos, según la información citada, provendrían de Estados Unidos.

data.title: Revelan cómo sigue Carlos Zelaya en México tras diagnóstico de cáncer
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Familiares del exdiputado Carlos Zelaya, hermano del expresidente hondureño Manuel Zelaya, dieron a conocer cómo se encuentra el exdiputado mientras continúa su tratamiento contra el cáncer en México. En el primer trimestre de este año se hizo público que Carlos Zelaya, conocido como “Carlón”, viajaba a México para recibir atención médica tras ser diagnosticado con cáncer de pulmón en etapa 4 metastásico. El también exsecretario del Congreso Nacional recibe tratamiento en el Instituto Nacional de Cancerología , ubicado en la Ciudad de México, donde se ha sometido a quimioterapias y monoterapias, según la información proporcionada. Recientemente, su sobrino Héctor Zelaya , exsecretario privado en la administración de Xiomara Castro (2002-2026), se refirió al estado de salud del exdiputado y señaló que continúa con su tratamiento médico. “Ahí está él con su tratamiento, siguiendo adelante y claro, hay que decir que la vida política, los políticos deterioran sus estados de salud por estar entregados ante una lucha popular...”, expresó Héctor Zelaya. Agregó que el exfuncionario necesita concentrarse en su recuperación para continuar con sus actividades. “Ahora le toca poner un poco de orden en su salud para poder seguir dando la lucha al lado del pueblo hondureño”, manifestó. Aunque las declaraciones confirman que Carlos Zelaya continúa recibiendo atención médica, no precisan si ha experimentado una mejoría clínica ni ofrecen detalles sobre los resultados de su tratamiento. De acuerdo con la información proporcionada, Carlos Zelaya fue diagnosticado con cáncer de pulmón en etapa 4 metastásico, una fase avanzada de la enfermedad en la que las células cancerosas se han extendido a otras partes del cuerpo. La información también señala que la enfermedad afectó los ganglios linfáticos y que el exdiputado ha presentado dificultades para hablar. Sin embargo, no se dispone de una declaración médica pública que detalle su condición actual ni la causa específica de ese síntoma. El tratamiento que recibe en México forma parte de la atención médica que ha buscado para enfrentar la enfermedad. El consumo de tabaco es uno de los principales factores de riesgo del cáncer de pulmón. Según la información proporcionada, Zelaya fue fumador durante muchos años; sin embargo, ese antecedente, por sí solo, no permite establecer la causa específica de su enfermedad. Recientemente, Carlos Zelaya también se reunió con su hermano, el expresidente Manuel Zelaya, quien viajó a México para recibir atención médica después de someterse a una operación de corazón. El encuentro se produjo mientras ambos recibían atención relacionada con sus respectivos problemas de salud. Por ahora, la familia ha señalado que Carlos Zelaya continúa adelante con su tratamiento, pero no ha ofrecido información médica detallada que permita establecer si su condición ha mejorado.

data.title: Cardenal Óscar Rodríguez pide a Honduras orar por la salud del papa León XIV
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. El cardenal de Honduras, Óscar Andrés Rodríguez , pidió este domingo intensificar las oraciones por la salud del papa León XIV tras el anuncio de que será sometido a una cirugía antes de iniciar una visita a Uruguay, Argentina y Perú en noviembre. Durante una homilía en la Basílica Menor de Suyapa, en Tegucigalpa, Rodríguez expresó su deseo de que el pontífice supere satisfactoriamente la operación a la que será sometido. "En todos estos días intensifiquemos nuestra oración por la salud de nuestro papa León XIV, que pueda salir muy bien de esa operación y que siga adelante guiando nuestra madre Iglesia", subrayó Rodríguez. Durante el tradicional rezo del Ángelus, el papa León XIV anunció que será intervenido quirúrgicamente en los próximos días debido a un nódulo pulmonar descubierto en una revisión médica. "Recientemente, durante algunos controles, los médicos me han encontrado un nódulo circunscrito en el pulmón. Ha sido detectado en una fase muy inicial y está bien localizado", declaró, siempre con tono sereno. El primer papa estadounidense de la historia, y con nacionalidad peruana por sus muchos años de misionero y obispo en el país andino, fue elegido en cónclave en mayo de 2025 para suceder a Francisco y acaba de cumplir 71 años, el pasado 14 de septiembre. Por el momento se sabe que esta primera operación como pontífice tendrá lugar en los próximos días de esta semana y que conllevará una hospitalización postoperatoria de cerca de una semana. La operación del pontífice, que implicará necesariamente suspender su agenda vaticana durante algunos días mientras se recupera, se produce a menos de un mes del viaje que tiene previsto realizar a Uruguay, Argentina y a Perú del 6 al 17 de noviembre.

data.title: Tercero al mando de la banda de El Mudo es enviado a prisión tras tercera captura
data.description: Cortés, Honduras. Tras ser capturado por tercera ocasión, Asahel Gonzales Aceituno , de 36 años, señalado por las autoridades como presunto tercero al mando de la banda de El Mudo, fue enviado a prisión preventiva tras un nuevo operativo policial en La Lima, Cortés. La captura se registró el viernes 9 de octubre , a las 5:50 de la tarde, durante labores de vigilancia y seguimiento, según el informe policial. La información trascendió este sábado 10 de octubre. Junto a Gonzales Aceituno fueron detenidos otros dos hombres y una mujer, investigados por su presunta vinculación con delitos relacionados con armas de fuego y asociación para delinquir. La Policía del Valle de Sula informó en sus redes sociales que un juez dictó detención preventiva contra los cuatro sospechosos. “Bajo resguardo policial son enviados a un centro penal de nuestro país”, indicó la institución. Gonzales Aceituno enfrenta señalamientos por tráfico de armas y asociación para delinquir. Las autoridades lo vinculan presuntamente con la banda de El Mudo, investigada por su supuesta participación en asaltos, robos y otros hechos violentos. El pasado martes 6 de octubre, Gonzales Aceituno había sido detenido por segunda vez en pocos días. Según la Policía, portaba un arma de fuego de uso comercial que no estaba registrada en el Registro Nacional Balístico. El comisionado César Ruiz, jefe regional de la Policía de Investigación en San Pedro Sula, informó entonces que el sospechoso tenía medidas judiciales impuestas desde 2023, entre ellas la prohibición de portar armas y de permanecer en lugares donde se consumieran bebidas alcohólicas. data.title: Honduras: buscan ampliar a L300,000 el límite de transacciones financieras
data.description: San Pedro Sula. Una modificación proyectada en la Tasa de Seguridad Poblacional busca incrementar el límite para determinadas operaciones financieras de personas naturales de 150,000 a 300,000 lempiras, medida orientada a impactar positivamente a hondureños con cuentas de ahorro. La iniciativa plantea modificar el límite asociado al cobro de dos lempiras por cada millar, según lo expuesto durante su presentación ante el Congreso Nacional. El cambio propuesto duplicaría el monto de referencia actual, aunque su aplicación dependerá de la aprobación de la reforma. La propuesta está orientada a las personas naturales que efectúan transacciones bancarias y busca ampliar el rango de operaciones contempladas en la disposición. “Esta iniciativa de ley lo que busca es beneficiar a una gran cantidad de hondureños, especialmente a las personas naturales”, manifestó el diputado nacionalista por Copán, Juan Carlos Lagos. Lagos explicó que la iniciativa fue presentada ante el pleno legislativo y que será remitida a la Secretaría del Congreso Nacional para continuar con el procedimiento correspondiente. Mientras no sea aprobada la reforma, el cambio no entra en vigor y se mantiene la normativa vigente. La propuesta busca elevar el límite de 150,000 a 300,000 lempiras, pero su alcance definitivo dependerá del contenido del proyecto y de la decisión que adopte el Congreso Nacional. La Tasa de Seguridad Poblacional fue creada mediante el Decreto 105-2011 para contribuir al financiamiento de programas e instituciones vinculados con la seguridad y la justicia. Desde su creación, el mecanismo ha estado sujeto a disposiciones legales que regulan su cobro y aplicación. Gracias a este tributo, en 2025 el gobierno recaudó 5,238.9 millones de lempiras , destinando el 54% —equivalente a 2,835 millones— a la Secretaría de Seguridad, y 14.2% —743 millones— a la Secretaría de Defensa .

data.title: El papa León XIV se operará de un nódulo en el pulmón
data.description: Ciudad del Vaticano. El papa León XIV anunció este domingo por sorpresa que en "los próximos días" deberá someterse a una operación por un nódulo en un pulmón en fase "muy inicial", a menos de un mes de su viaje apostólico a Uruguay, Argentina y Perú. Ha sido el propio pontífice quien ha informado sobre su salud de forma pública, desde la ventana del palacio apostólico tras el rezo del Ángelus y ante miles de fieles que le escuchaban desde la plaza de San Pedro. "Recientemente, durante algunos controles, los médicos me han encontrado un nódulo circunscrito en el pulmón. Ha sido detectado en una fase muy inicial y está bien localizado", declaró, en tono sereno. Acto seguido, aclaró que los médicos "consideran oportuno intervenir" y por ello, siguiendo sus consejos, finalmente ha decidido "operarse para extirpar" el nódulo "en los próximos días". Su mensaje suscitó el aplauso de los fieles en la plaza: "Os agradezco vuestra cercanía espiritual y me encomiendo a vuestra oración. Gracias y buen domingo", terminó, saludando con la mano desde la ventana antes de desaparecer y volver al palacio. El primer papa estadounidense de la historia, y con nacionalidad peruana por sus muchos años de misionero y obispo en el país andino, fue elegido en cónclave en mayo de 2025 para suceder a Francisco y acaba de cumplir 71 años, el pasado 14 de septiembre. Por el momento se sabe que esta primera operación como pontífice tendrá lugar en los próximos días de esta semana y que conllevará una hospitalización postoperatoria de cerca de una semana. "En respuesta a las preguntas de los periodistas, puedo precisar que la intervención está prevista para los primeros días de la próxima semana y que el tiempo previsto de hospitalización postoperatoria es de aproximadamente una semana", indicó en una breve comunicación el portavoz vaticano, Matteo Bruni. La intervención está prevista en el hospital Agostino Gemelli de Roma, donde el Vaticano cuenta con un apartamento privado desde los años ochenta, en tiempos de Juan Pablo II. La operación del pontífice, que implicará necesariamente suspender su agenda vaticana mientras se recupera, se produce a menos de un mes del viaje que tiene previsto realizar a Uruguay, Argentina y a Perú del 6 al 17 de noviembre. Sin embargo, sus palabras este domingo en el Ángelus, justo antes de sorprender al mundo con esta noticia, sugieren que su gira latinoamericana sigue en pie. Poco antes del anuncio, León XIV dedicó un saludo especial a un grupo de personas que habían llevado a la plaza de San Pedro del Vaticano un altar del Señor de los Milagros, muy venerado en Perú. "Saludo a los miembros de la Hermandad del Señor de los Milagros en Roma y a todos aquellos que han participado en la procesión con el venerado icono del Crucificado", apreció. Y, acto seguido, aseguró: "Gracias por vuestra oración por la visita pastoral que llevaré a cabo en Perú". La primera en reaccionar a la noticia de la operación del papa ha sido la primera ministra italiana, Giorgia Meloni , quien expresó su apoyo personal y el de su gobierno ante su próxima hospitalización. Pero también destacó la "tranquilidad" con la que realizó el anuncio ante el mundo. "Su serenidad y tranquilidad durante el Ángelus nos reconfortan. Estoy segura de que el pueblo italiano también le brindará todo su apoyo y afecto", destacó.

data.title: Onda tropical en Honduras: zonas en las que lloverá este domingo
data.description: ​​​​​​San Pedro Sula, Honduras. Las precipitaciones asociadas al paso de una onda tropical mantienen bajo vigilancia a distintas regiones de Honduras, ante la posibilidad de que aumenten los caudales de ríos y quebradas y se produzcan inundaciones o deslizamientos. El fenómeno ingresará acompañado de humedad, un factor que favorecerá la formación de lluvias en distintos puntos del territorio. Los sectores norte y central figuran entre las áreas donde se esperan precipitaciones, aunque las condiciones podrían extenderse a otras regiones del país, informó la Secretaría de Gestión de Riesgos y Contingencias Nacionales ( Copeco ) Además de las inundaciones y los movimientos de tierra, las lluvias podrían ocasionar la caída de árboles y otros incidentes, principalmente en comunidades expuestas a este tipo de amenazas. Copeco ha establecido alertas en distintos sectores como parte de las acciones ante las condiciones lluviosas. En materia de temperaturas, el oriente hondureño registrará uno de los valores más altos, con máximas de 34 °C. En la zona norte se esperan hasta 33 °C, mientras que en el área insular el termómetro podría alcanzar los 32 °C, con mínimas de 27 °C. Para la región central se pronostican temperaturas de hasta 31 °C y mínimas de 19 °C. En el Distrito Central , los registros oscilarán entre los 19 y 30 °C, mientras que en el occidente se prevén condiciones más frescas, con máximas de 30 °C y mínimas de 15 °C. Ante la posibilidad de crecidas repentinas, las autoridades instan a evitar el cruce de ríos y quebradas cuando presenten corrientes fuertes, así como a mantenerse alejados de laderas inestables y zonas susceptibles a inundaciones. También recomiendan consultar los avisos oficiales para conocer los cambios en las condiciones meteorológicas y las disposiciones vigentes en cada localidad.

data.title: Irán acusa a Trump de recurrir al miedo por decir que puede destruir ciudades de EEUU
data.description: Teherán, Irán. Irán acusó al presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , de recurrir a la “política del miedo” después de que el mandatario estadounidense afirmara esta semana durante un mitin electoral que el país persa podría “destruir” Los Ángeles y San Diego. “Este es un ejemplo de manual de la política del miedo: aterrorizar a la gente con una amenaza imaginaria, presentar la destrucción de sus propias ciudades como un precio aceptable”, dijo el portavoz del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores iraní, Esmaeil Baqaei , en su cuenta de X a última hora del sábado. Según el diplomático, las declaraciones de Trump y su afirmación de que la destrucción de Los Ángeles y San Diego sería “un precio muy pequeño que pagar” buscan “desviar la atención del verdadero peligro” que es la “cúpula gobernante (de EE.UU.) que ha impuesto al mundo una guerra ilegal con consecuencias globales”. Baqaei responde así a los comentarios de Trump durante un mitin celebrado el lunes en Nebraska, que provocaron críticas de políticos demócratas y republicanos de California. "Podrían destruir una ciudad. Que destruyan Los Ángeles, que destruyan San Diego", declaró el mandatario: "Este es un precio muy pequeño a pagar, y todo habrá terminado muy pronto», dijo el presidente estadounidense durante un mitin electoral. Tras la polémica, Trump atribuyó el jueves a las “noticias falsas” la polémica y aclaró en su red Truth Social que se refería al aumento temporal del precio de la gasolina como un coste asumible para impedir que Irán obtenga un arma nuclear. En las últimas semanas, el presidente republicano ha pasado de amenazar con “aniquilar” a Irán durante su intervención ante Naciones Unidas a asegurar hace tres días que no lanzará nuevos ataques contra el país persa antes de las elecciones legislativas estadounidenses del 3 de noviembre, al afirmar que mantiene contactos “productivos” con Teherán. Por su parte, el ministro iraní de Exteriores, Abás Araqchí, afirmó el mismo jueves que su país responderá en unos días a la última propuesta de Washington para poner fin a la guerra y confirmó que los contactos entre ambas partes continúan a través de intermediarios. Mientras tanto, ambos países mantienen su pulso por el estrecho de Ormuz, después de que las fuerzas estadounidenses atacaran anoche un buque comercial procedente de Irán en el golfo de Omán en el marco de su bloqueo naval, y de que la Guardia Revolucionaria anunciara el día anterior un ataque contra un buque que transportaba gas licuado y reiterara su control sobre esta ruta estratégica.

data.title: Feriado Morazánico 2026 cerró con tres muertos, dos por ahogamiento y uno en accidente vial
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras.- La Semana Morazánica finalizó y la Comisión Nacional de Prevención en Movilizaciones Masivas ( Conapremm ) oficializó las incidencias reportadas durante el feriado de 2026. Según Conapremm, se reportaron tres muertes relacionadas con la movilización durante el Feriado Morazánico 2026: dos por ahogamiento y una en un accidente vial. Las cifras negativas disminuyeron en comparación con otros años, según informó Nelson Márquez, viceministro de la Secretaría de Estado en los Despachos de Gestión de Riesgos y Contingencias Nacionales (Copeco). Durante una conferencia de prensa, las autoridades confirmaron que el operativo contó con la participación de 23 instituciones, 1,384 puntos de control, 187 puntos de control turístico y más de 300 unidades de ambulancia desplegadas en diferentes puntos del país. Según el reporte brindado por Yanci López, representante de la Cruz Roja Hondureña, la institución habilitó más de 200 puestos de socorro y brindó más de 600 servicios, entre primeros auxilios, traslados, atención psicosocial y asistencia médica. También se reportaron 17 rescates acuáticos realizados por los equipos de la institución en coordinación con otras entidades. Por su parte, el general Marco Antonio Artica, comandante del Cuerpo de Bomberos, informó que realizaron nueve rescates acuáticos y brindaron más de 400 servicios de ambulancia. Las Fuerzas Armadas también formaron parte de los operativos y brindaron más de 300 atenciones médicas. Además, habilitaron áreas de descanso y talleres mecánicos móviles para asistir a los viajeros. Héctor Ordóñez, ministro de Comunicaciones, confirmó que 33,000 voluntarios se sumaron a las labores de Conapremm durante el Feriado Morazánico. Las autoridades no confirmaron la cantidad de turistas que se movilizaron durante el feriado, debido a que todavía había personas desplazándose por diferentes puntos del país al momento de brindar el informe.
